fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is asymptotically blocked by lattice arithmetic. If p and q are two nearest legal points, every p+j(q-p) is a lattice point; with a fixed-size alphabet, an outside point occurs for constant j and remains only a constant-factor farther, so no polynomial shell ratio follows.

Proposal 2 is the sole conditional survivor, but its stated BCH/expander experiment omits the essential completeness audit. Any syndrome check valid for every honest encoding must annihilate their difference span, which may already contain the G5, three-term, parity, or deletion attacks; code distance alone does not exclude this.

Proposal 3 cannot enforce canonical signed digits using linear recurrence rows alone; alternative integer digits and carries remain lattice points. Repeating a chain also repeats honest baseline cost, so a sparse defect gains no polynomial relative gap absent a separate zero-baseline theorem.

Proposal 4 supplies neither an explicit configuration nor the claimed Graver dichotomy. Honest-assignment affine spans can generate constant-support non-honest combinations, exactly the type already witnessed by the overlap and parity kernels.

Proposal 5 fails because incidence treewidth and well-linkedness do not locate the unsatisfiable core. A low-width contradictory appendage can be attached to an irrelevant high-width satisfiable component, leaving routed attack cost local.

Proposal 6's pure tensor claim is false for deletion amplification. For base target t and legal point u, normalized legal squared distance at depth d is 1+(||u||²/||t||²)^d-2(<t,u>/||t||²)^d; by Cauchy-Schwarz this cannot decay polynomially relative to deletion for fixed nonidentical base vectors.

Proposal 7 has Θ(m^k) honest tuple baseline but only Θ(m^(k-1)) tuples containing one false clause, so fixed-k replication does not itself improve the normalized gap. Fixed-level marginal systems also admit locally consistent signed pseudo-distributions, leaving the claimed global soundness theorem absent.
evidence: Generation 5 found a squared-norm-at-most-4 kernel move in every one of 5,832 tested overlap systems and 95,256 references, contradicting proposals that merely assert global coupling removes G5.

Generation 7 emitted the unrestricted lattice and found the exact zero-residual three-term attack at squared distance 80 versus baseline 72; residual scaling or radix processing cannot detect such a kernel.

Generations 9 and 11 found constant-cost seven-term parity kernels, including one hidden by a uniquely occurring cubic moment. Proposal 2 has not shown that completeness-compatible code checks detect either kernel.

Generation 12 exactly found clause deletion at 105 versus the required 108, despite charging parity to 153. Assertions that zero blocks or deletion automatically become expensive require explicit unrestricted verification.
All supplied positive results are finite; no verifier establishes a uniform family, composition theorem, code compatibility theorem, or dimension-dependent gap.

For each p in {2,3,5}, form D_p as the span of differences of all 16 globally consistent one-hot encodings on the current 72 selectors, use the maximal compatible syndrome space D_p orthogonal, and exhaustively test all supplied G5 circuits, G7 three-term attacks, G9/G11 parities, G12 clause drops, and every non-honest deviation through anchor excess 36. Kill the raw-selector coding line if every prime retains a harmful zero-syndrome vector; a prime survives only if all consistent encodings are accepted and every audited attack has nonzero syndrome.
